invariant: unscreened Bash or read output is never treated as Firstmate truth
why: it cannot withhold on Claude, so it reported itself as protection it did not provide; the note it appended was advisory only
replaced_by: nothing; the same invariant is carried by the human review of tool output and by jev-pretool-deny for actions, not reads

invariant: a shell command that Jev judges irreversible or destructive never runs
why: its effect and destructive-intent questions ask for the decision itself, so a worker's own cleanup reads as destructive: 63 of its 69 refusals were false positives, and eval or python -c bypassed it
replaced_by: nothing yet; OS-level write confinement of each worker process tree, with the delegated-write residual named, is the planned replacement

invariant: a shell command whose required Jev judgment could not run never runs
why: it only failed the retired shell model gate closed; it turned provider failures into refusals of harmless commands, including a worker's own inbox acknowledgement (O13)
replaced_by: nothing; a shell call now needs no judgment, so there is no judgment to wait for

invariant: during a failed shell judgment only a proven read-only command or a lab-home command runs
why: the read-only classifier and the lab-home marker existed only to stop the retired shell outage denial from refusing legitimate work, and no ledger row ever used either branch
replaced_by: nothing; with no shell judgment and no shell outage denial there is nothing left to admit

invariant: untrusted tool output never becomes an omp worker's authority
why: data/fm-jev-guard-e2e/report.md sections 3.2, 3.5 and 7.4: 0 true positives in a random sample of 70 of its withholds, no third-party source among 3,431 traced withholds, 29% of omp bash outputs hidden, and Claude workers never had it
replaced_by: nothing; tool results reach the worker unchanged, and third-party input, if one is ever added, is labelled by source at the tool boundary

invariant: a read of bytes the task owns skips the result screen
why: data/fm-jev-guard-e2e/report.md sections 3.2 and 7.4: an exemption that existed only to keep the result screen off task-owned reads; it never refused anything
replaced_by: nothing; with no result screen there is nothing to exempt

invariant: a launch or steering record whose receipt matches skips the result screen
why: data/fm-jev-guard-e2e/report.md sections 3.2, 7.4 and 8: it only exempted a consistent record from screening and never refused a forged one, so its publisher receipts had no other consumer
replaced_by: nothing; launch and steering records reach the worker unchanged and their publishers write no receipt

invariant: a local AXI tool's own help lines are excluded from the result screen
why: data/fm-jev-guard-e2e/report.md sections 3.2 and 7.4: a command list, omp trailer match and wall-time allowance that existed only to keep the result screen from withholding local tool help
replaced_by: nothing; local tool output, help lines included, reaches the worker unchanged

invariant: an omp tool result too large to screen completely is withheld
why: data/fm-jev-guard-e2e/report.md sections 3.2, 3.6 and 7.4: the result half of the size refusal withheld large outputs only because the result screen could not cover them; the pre-tool size refusal is unchanged
replaced_by: nothing; large results reach the worker unchanged
